To represent the theory of evolution as (subject, predicate, object) triples, I have categorized the information into core mechanisms, historical foundations, and supporting evidence.

### I. Core Mechanisms (Darwinian Principles)
1. (Individual organisms, exhibit, phenotypic variation)
2. (Resources, are, limited)
3. (Population growth, outpaces, resource availability)
4. (Natural selection, favors, advantageous traits)
5. (Advantageous traits, increase, reproductive success)
6. (Offspring, inherit, genetic material)
7. (Reproduction, transmits, favorable alleles)
8. (Time, accumulates, genetic changes)
9. (Adaptation, improves, environmental fit)

### II. Molecular Genetics (The Modern Synthesis)
1. (DNA, stores, hereditary information)
2. (Mutations, generate, new alleles)
3. (Meiosis, increases, genetic diversity)
4. (Gene flow, moves, alleles between populations)
5. (Genetic drift, causes, random frequency shifts)
6. (Allele frequencies, change, over generations)
7. (Phenotype, results from, genotype-environment interaction)

### III. Macroevolution and Speciation
1. (Speciation, requires, reproductive isolation)
2. (Geographic barriers, prevent, gene flow)
3. (Common ancestors, give rise to, divergent lineages)
4. (Phylogenetic trees, represent, evolutionary relationships)
5. (Extinction, removes, less-fit lineages)
6. (Adaptive radiation, fills, ecological niches)

### IV. Evidence and Observation
1. (Fossil records, document, transitional forms)
2. (Comparative anatomy, reveals, homologous structures)
3. (Vestigial organs, indicate, ancestral functions)
4. (Embryology, demonstrates, developmental similarities)
5. (Biogeography, explains, species distribution)
6. (DNA sequencing, quantifies, genetic relatedness)
7. (Observed microevolution, confirms, natural selection in real-time)

### V. Conceptual Framework
1. (Evolution, defines, change over time)
2. (The Theory of Evolution, unifies, biological sciences)
3. (Evolution, lacks, teleological goals)
4. (Fitness, measures, reproductive output)
5. (Survival, facilitates, gene transmission)
